_policy: Every consciously deferred piece of work gets a row: what was deferred, why, what enforcement exists meanwhile, and a review-by date. `cargo xtask deferrals --check` (weekly scheduled CI) fails once a row passes its date un-re-decided — a deferral nobody re-examines is a silent forever. Re-deciding means either building the thing (delete the row) or re-dating it with a fresh reason in the same commit. Decisions intended to be permanent do not belong here; they get ADRs.

deferrals.what: Re-decided 2026-06-27 — do NOT file the 'add POST-path resumption' fix. The 2026-07-28 draft removes SSE stream resumability and Last-Event-ID from Streamable HTTP (register 1.5d Major #9, SEP-2575), so that fix is obsoleted by the spec. Re-scoped to the durable residue: assess whether rmcp's hang on early POST-stream close (instead of surfacing a re-issuable error, which the new text REQUIRES) is worth filing — judged against the FINAL spec text plus the draft suite's transport/sse scenarios
deferrals.why: The original premise (2025-11-25 requires the Last-Event-ID resumption rmcp lacks on the POST path) is being deleted by 2026-07-28; filing the add-resumption fix now would ask upstream to build a mechanism the next revision removes, while upstream is already implementing the removal (register 3.11). The re-scoped hang question cannot be verified until the final text ships (2026-07-28) and the draft suite scenarios stabilize
deferrals.meanwhile: Register rows 3.12 + 1.5d carry the reconciliation; the dossier (docs/reports/rmcp-sse-resumption-dossier.md) records that the spec removes the requirement and re-scopes to the hang. The 2025-11-25 mechanism remains exact — re-verified first-hand 2026-06-27 at rmcp head eb435c6 (raw_sse_to_jsonrpc l.303 'without reconnection logic'; POST arms l.778-779/803-804; SseAutoReconnectStream GET-only at l.584/720) — and the reference host still passes sse-retry 3/3, so the evidence is preserved if the decision reopens

deferrals.what: Adopt rmcp 1.8.0+ for the enumNames fix (rust-sdk#905) as a DELIBERATE upgrade WITH conformance re-validation, folded into the M2.5 2026-07-28 migration. NOT the clean minor bump it looked like: an attempt on 2026-07-19 (bumped 1.7.0->1.8.0, flipped the roundtrip.rs enumNames assertion to preserved — that part worked) was REVERTED because 1.8.0 bundles two more behavior changes. When adopting: drop the roundtrip.rs loss-pin + interactive.rs notes, add the #[allow(deprecated)] sites, decide the arg-error semantics, MOVE THE rmcp-macros CEILING SHIM in crates/mcp-everything-server/Cargo.toml to the new minor (register 3.13 — it is a hard constraint, so a stale bound blocks resolution loudly rather than breaking the build subtly), update register 3.8/3.10/3.13. 2026-07-26: the target is now a three-way choice, not a bump — 1.8.0, 2.2.0 (current stable; Dependabot PR #28 proposes it and produces ~70 compile errors), or the 3.0.x line that implements 2026-07-28 (register 3.1); picking the 3.0.x line makes this deferral and the M2.5 registry work one piece of work
deferrals.why: 1.8.0 is inseparable from: (a) SEP-2577 forward-deprecation of Roots/Sampling/Logging — features active and REQUIRED for our 2025-11-25 conformance surface, needing ~7 #[allow(deprecated)] sites across mcp-everything-server + mcp-reference-host; and (b) a semantics change where tool-argument-deserialization failures return a tool-error result (isError:true) instead of an MCP protocol error (-32602), which broke 3 arg-validation tests. (b) is conformance-relevant and CANNOT be validated locally (needs the npx conformance gate), so reactively patching tests around it risks masking a 40/40 regression. This belongs in a deliberate upgrade with full suite re-validation, not a hygiene bump
deferrals.meanwhile: Pinned rmcp 1.7.0; tests/roundtrip.rs still pins the enumNames loss and fails LOUDLY the moment a bumped rmcp preserves it, forcing this work; register 3.8 records the release confirmation AND the 2026-07-19 bump-attempt findings. The M2.5 migration will upgrade rmcp deliberately and re-run the conformance gate, which is where these three changes get handled together
